description: memory.rs:596 (`position as usize`), :598 (`position.saturating_neg() as usize`), and :604 (`n as usize` on the limit) are all silent lossy casts. The i64→usize casts are flagged by `clippy::cast_possible_truncation` (32-bit targets) and `clippy::cast_sign_loss` (positive-i64 reading). The u64→usize cast on `limit` is also `cast_possible_truncation` on 32-bit. — Idiomatic Rust uses `usize::try_from(...)` with explicit fallback (saturating_to_usize-style helpers, or a single `#[allow(clippy::cast_possible_truncation)]` with a // SAFETY: comment justifying the platform assumption). Even on 64-bit-only deployments, these casts read as 'author skipped the check' rather than 'author considered the check'. Engineering impact: a 32-bit consumer of this reference impl gets silent wrong results on positions/limits over 2^31.
title: Lossy as-cast cluster in query_objects: i64→usize, u64→usize without try_from
